_comment: Reasoned exemptions from the G5-U untranslated-source check in tools/check_catalog_parity.py: msgids whose translation is legitimately byte-identical to its English source. Most such strings need no entry, because the checker recognises them structurally -- a source with no translatable word once its {placeholders}, `code spans`, URLs, digits, punctuation, single letters and NON_TRANSLATABLE_TERMS are removed. This file is for the judgements a pattern cannot make: a borrowed word, a proper noun the term list does not carry, a string a translator has decided reads better untranslated. It lives beside the catalogs, not in Python, because docs/I18N.md promises a contributor adding a locale never edits Python. Every entry needs a written reason, and the checker deletes nothing for you: an entry whose msgid the template no longer declares, whose locale is not checked, or whose translation has since been translated fails the gate until it is removed. A list that only grows stops describing the catalogs and starts describing the project's history. It is empty today because all four identical strings in en/es (n, the em dash, and the two pure-placeholder web values) are structurally exempt.
